assertion_audit.fails_if: Dispatch reuses a run ID, drops a claimant, or rejects the second shared-root dispatch; restoring the exclusive default fails before these assertions.
Admission holds the shared-root request, omits its launch result, or leaves its pointer queued; restoring root-unaware membership produces held-on-claim.
The exclusive refusal names another owner or omits the configured pattern; removing exclusive precedence fails the surrounding raises context.
A directory or no-roots refusal names another run; admitting those overlaps fails the surrounding raises contexts.
Legacy explicit sharing refuses the second dispatch or yields no run ID.
Queue edit skips the directory holder or identifies the wrong holder; restoring its broad shared-path skip makes refusal None.
Admission skips the directory holder or fails to name it; restoring its broad shared-path skip makes hold None.
Queue edit rejects an exact shared-root co-claim; restoring root-unaware membership returns a conflict.
Either queue guard admits an exclusive collision or omits its configured pattern from the refusal.
Root membership fails for an existing source, existing extensionless file, future file or root-only declaration.
Membership allows a root directory, absent suffixless directory, existing dotted directory, sibling root or escaping path.
Root membership overrides the private subtree exclusion or the diagnostic returns a different or absent exclusive pattern.

assertion_independence: No tautological added assertion found: configuration values are checked against separately computed decisions or messages, claimant identities come from independent dispatch outputs, and membership checks contain positive and negative controls.
